cards.title: Evidence never speaks for itself
cards.body: After every piece of evidence, explain what it shows and why it matters: “This shows that…”, “This means…”, “That matters because…”. Repeating the evidence is not an explanation.

cards.title: Topic, evidence, explanation, link
cards.text: Phones keep families in touch during the school day. For example, a parent can text when pick-up plans change. This means students aren’t left waiting outside with no ride. Being able to reach family is one reason phones belong at lunch.
cards.note: Topic sentence → example → explanation → a link back to the thesis.

cards.title: The body paragraph builder
cards.body: Use the builder to plan: a topic sentence, two pieces of evidence each with its explanation, and a closing sentence. Then put it in your writing and polish it. The essay map marks the topic sentence and the kind of evidence.

prompts: Read your explanations. Do they say something new, or repeat the evidence?
Which piece of evidence was strongest? Why?
